entities.name: Pierre de la Vergne
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pierre de la Vergne (also Pierre de Veruche, Verneyo, Veruco, Verrujo, or Veroche; Latin Petrus de Vernio) was a fourteenth-century French churchman who rose into the college of cardinals during the Avignon Papacy. Like many clerics of the period, he is documented under shifting vernacular and Latin spellings that reflect curial chancery practice and later antiquarian confusion.

His career belongs to the Avignon system's preference for legally trained French and Limousin clerics who staffed tribunals, collected revenues, and advised popes amid the Babylonian Captivity of the Church. Cardinal creations in this milieu bound regional ecclesiastical elites to the papal court on the Rhône, shaping benefice distribution across France.

Though not a household name beside popes such as Clement VI or Gregory XI, Pierre de la Vergne illustrates how Avignon cardinalate networks operated: multilingual naming, legal service, and integration of provincial clergy into a supra-diocesan papal monarchy that preceded the Western Schism's crisis of obedience.
